reel.title: Kyiv: Russian warship sunk 2,400 km from the front | Wider war or isolated strikes?
reel.hook: KYIV: RUSSIAN WARSHIP SUNK [2,400 KM] FROM THE FRONT
reel.topic: Ukraine's sea-drone strike on Russian ships at Benghazi, Libya, on Sunday 22 Nov, and why oil did not react. Zelenskyy, in a post on X on Monday 23 Nov: seven domestically made naval drones were used, 'the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk' (commissioned in 2023), a Ka-27 helicopter was destroyed and the cargo ship Angara was hit (CBS/AP, Middle East Eye, RFE/RL, The Moscow Times; AP via The American Legion). The ship was docked at the Benghazi Naval Base, about 2,400 km from the front line (AP, Middle East Eye; CBS: some 1,500 miles). Two Libyan military officials told AP that at least four drones were intercepted and two struck the vessel, and that an initial investigation suggests the drones were launched from a facility run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya (AFP via Gulf News: 'not independently established'; The Moscow Times). Ukraine's SBU says they were launched from a 'mothership' near the target and calls both ships legitimate military targets (CBS/AP, Middle East Eye, RFE/RL). Satellite images from Vantor show the ship capsized in port (CBS: Vantor via Reuters; MEE: Vantor/AFP; RFE/RL); BBC Verify saw a vessel on fire at 05:47 GMT in Planet Labs images and later partly submerged. Russia: the Kremlin referred questions to the Defense Ministry (Peskov: 'Our defense ministry is handling this', RBC-Ukraine; CBS/AP; RFE/RL); 'Russia has not officially commented on the loss of the Merkury' (The Moscow Times, page updated 24 Nov 09:28 Moscow time; CBS updated 23 Nov 8:20 PM EST). Libya: the eastern government (backed by Khalifa Haftar's forces, which have ties with Russia, MEE; RFE/RL) said the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies under a maritime agreement with Russia (BBC, AFP, MEE), called the strike a violation of Libya's sovereignty (AFP, RFE/RL, RBC-Ukraine) and asked the UN for an international investigation (MEE, RBC-Ukraine); Tripoli's foreign ministry said the war 'gives neither side the right to conduct military operations on Libyan territory' (RFE/RL) and its government warned against involving ports in outside conflicts (BBC); Libyan officials told AP earlier this year that Ukrainian drone specialists work in western Libya (CBS/AP). The UN mission, UNSMIL: 'serious concern', an 'immediate, independent and transparent investigation', and Libya 'cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts' (CBS/AP, MEE, AFP, RFE/RL). The day before, Saturday 21 Nov: drones hit the US-sanctioned Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland; Finland's military said it was likely a Ukrainian strike, Kyiv has neither confirmed nor denied it, and Peskov called it 'indeed a very dangerous trend' (CBS/AP; The Moscow Times). Oil: Reuters says prices fell on Monday as flows from the Middle East rose and Libya's Sharara pipeline reopened (Reuters via MarineLink); Libya's National Oil Corporation said an 'unlawful group' ('outlaws' in Xinhua) had shut a valve, threatening about 350,000 barrels a day, and that the line reopened after about 10 hours, with crude reaching the Akakus tanks at Zawiya, about 50 km west of Tripoli; Sharara is Libya's largest oil field, in the Murzuq Basin in the south-west, and oil is about 90% of the economy (Xinhua, Hydrocarbon Processing). None of the oil reports links the pipeline to the strike, and the Reel does not either.
